Help us build the next generation of lifting and transport equipment for the wind industry

We're looking for an experienced Automation Engineer who wants to take responsibility for control systems, PLC software and machine automation.

This is a newly established role at Danhydra, where you will help strengthen automation across future products and development projects.

The role

Some days you will be working with PLC software and control architecture. Other days you may be reviewing functional safety requirements, troubleshooting on a test setup, supporting commissioning activities, or discussing technical solutions with suppliers and colleagues from production and engineering.

You will work closely with colleagues within hydraulics, mechanics and electrical engineering to develop robust and reliable machine control solutions.

Your responsibilities

•    Develop PLC and HMI software using Siemens TIA Portal

•    Define automation concepts and system architecture for new products

•    Translate functional and safety requirements into practical control solutions

•    Support testing, troubleshooting and commissioning activities

•    Specify and integrate sensors, electrical components and control hardware

•    Work closely with colleagues within hydraulics, mechanics and electrical engineering

•    Contribute to machine safety design and compliance with Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

•    Support technical dialogue with suppliers and development partners

What we're looking for

You have experience from industrial machinery, mobile equipment, automation systems or similar technical environments.

You have worked with systems where software, hydraulics, electrical components and mechanics need to work together reliably under demanding operating conditions.

We expect that you:

•    Have experience with Siemens PLCs and TIA Portal

•    Understand industrial control systems and machine automation

•    Can translate functional requirements into practical control solutions

•    Work well across different engineering disciplines

•    Take responsibility for your work and follow tasks through to completion

Experience with hydraulic control systems, proportional valves, pressure and flow control, or closed-loop regulation will be considered a strong advantage.

Why join Danhydra?

At Danhydra, we develop and manufacture specialised lifting, transportation and installation equipment used throughout the global wind industry.

With more than 25 years of experience in the wind industry and approximately 160 employees across Denmark, Germany, Spain, India and the United States, we continue to develop equipment that helps customers handle some of the industry's largest and most demanding components.

You will join a team where technical decisions are made close to the engineering work and where practical solutions matter.

We review applications continuously and will conduct interviews until we find the right candidate.

If you would like to learn more about the position, please apply.

Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

   

  Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applicants for PhD stipends in mathematics.

  The start date is ordinarily September 1, 2027, but can be subject to negotiation.

  There will be PhD stipends available in:

   	
• Algebraic and Arithmetic Geometry, Applied algebra, Combinatorics, Geometric group theory, Geometry and Geometric Analysis, Number Theory, Representation Theory, and Topology as covered by the section Algebra & Geometry and  Copenhagen Center for Geometry & Topology (GeoTop).    	
• Classical Analysis, Descriptive Set Theory, Functional Analysis, Geometric group theory, Harmonic Analysis, History of Mathematics, Mathematical Physics, Operator Algebras, Partial Differential Equations, Quantum Information, Quantum Computation and Quantum Simulation as covered by the section Analysis and Quantum, the Centre for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory  and the Quantum for Life Center.   You are welcome to contact any member of the department to discuss research projects.

   

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the field of Mathematics or nearby fields, whose background and research interests are a strong fit with the areas of mathematics above.

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members; around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics, and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website http://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research  conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/.  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  You can find more information about the PhD program on the homepage http://www.math.ku.dk/english/programmes/ph.d/. 

   

  The PhD programme 

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. mathematics or closely related. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled in one of the faculty’s master’s programmes in Mathematics or Quantum Information Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme  (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional experience, including publications (if any) 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics 	
• Good English skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, publications (if any), language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or Master’s and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Reference letters (if available; letters can be uploaded as part of the application or sent to hr-math@adm.ku.dk by the reference person).   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 GMT+1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**We are looking for several Lead Business Consultants to join our EMEA Consulting Services team, working with our clients across the UK and the Nordics. Our client base in the region is growing, and so is the breadth of expertise our implementation projects require. Rather than hiring for one narrow profile, we are opening multiple positions for implementation specialists across the full front-to-back platform, and we will match you to the projects where your depth is strongest.

The team allows for consulting excellency, efficiency in configuration and standardization as well as knowledge sharing and collaboration across divisions and market units. As a Lead Business Consultant you are, or will become, a trusted business and technology advisor for our clients in one or more of the following areas:

• Investment accounting and financial reporting (ABOR)

• Investment book of record (IBOR), position keeping and valuation

• Investment operations, settlement and post-trade processing

• Data management, interfaces and communications (Data & Com)

• Front office: portfolio management, trading and order management

• Compliance, regulatory and internal restrictions

• Performance measurement and attribution

• Risk management (market and liquidity)

• Alternative investments and private markets

• Instrument valuation and analytics (theoretical pricing)

You will be exposed to the complete spectrum of financial instruments and their valuation, from plain vanilla equity and fixed income instruments to complex OTC derivatives and private market assets. Furthermore, you will work with all processes related to your area of specialization.

As part of your induction you will be ‘hands-on’ in our software system and attend the three-weeks’ SimCorp Dimension® Academy.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**As a Lead Business Consultant you will take over a range of tasks in a project team, such as:

• Be responsible for major parts of SimCorp implementation projects in your area of specialisation: you anticipate client needs based on your understanding of the relevant business processes at asset managers, asset owners, insurers or banks and act as a trusted advisor to the client

• Design and configure solutions across multiple modules and project streams that enable our clients to reach their desired outcomes

• Connect your specialism to the wider front-to-back solution, working closely with colleagues who cover the adjacent areas of the platform

• Advise on and improve standard implementation processes as well as product and service offerings

• Identify opportunities for growth and explore new ideas, feeding this back to the organisation and supporting its development

• Participate in sales processes when required to position SimCorp concepts and offerings

• Instruct and mentor less experienced colleagues on the job and share knowledge with colleagues on an international level

**What We Value

**You like to deep dive into business processes in investment management and enjoy modelling them in our software. You have in-depth knowledge about the business at asset managers, fund managers, insurers or banks. In addition you bring with you:

• Degree in economics, finance, mathematics, computer science or similar qualification

• Previous experience as an Analyst or (Implementation) Consultant for asset managers, asset owners, banks or consulting firms

• FRM, CFA, CIPM or other relevant certifications/designations are desirable

• Team spirit and a desire to share your knowledge

• High communication and consulting skills

• High degree of commercial awareness, customer orientation and quality consciousness

• Fluency in English

• Readiness to travel

**Benefits

**SimCorp provides a range of benefits that may influence decisions regarding job offers. With operations in more than 30 offices globally, the benefits package can differ depending on the country. SimCorp implements a global hybrid work policy, requiring employees to be in the office two days per week and permitting remote work on other days. Additional information about location-specific benefits is available from the recruiter.

The role is a full-time position and reports to the Head of Procure to Pay.

**

• Lead, coach and develop a team of 7 FTEs across the Accounts Payable function.

• Approve journals and oversee approval of new vendors and vendor changes.

• Own the monthly close process for Accounts Payable, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery.

• Manage and delegate audit deliverables across quarterly, interim, and yearly cycles.

• Maintain control and oversight of the supplier invoice workflow, including monitoring and clearing backlog to keep processing on track.

• Own KPI reporting and performance tracking, providing visibility to the Head of P2P and key stakeholders.

• Drive continuous improvement, leading automation and process projects to move the function towards scalable, less manual ways of working.

• Ensure adherence to company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements, maintaining strong governance within the AP function.

**KEY EXPECTATIONS

**In this role, you take full ownership of your team's output and workload distribution, manage complex operational and people challenges, and drive process improvement across the function. You lead rather than execute - setting direction, removing blockers, and holding the team accountable to a high standard. Qualia is the company that brings foundation models into the real world: data collection, fine-tuning, inference, and on-device deployment, end to end. We're a small, technical team in Copenhagen and Stockholm building this for manufacturers, in partnership with top companies. Qualia has raised roughly USD 10M to pursue the hardest problems in robotics.

We're hiring a research engineer to push the model side of our research. VLAs, WAMs, that work on real customer data. RL that closes the gap on precision tasks. World models, UMI, EgoData, that let us iterate faster than collecting another 1,000 episodes of teleop.

This is not a research role at a lab. This is a research engineer role at a startup. Your work ships to customers, runs on robots, and gets judged by whether the task succeeds.

What you'll work on

• VLA fine-tuning at the edge of what's possible

• VLAs on customer and internal data. Make them work where the base model fails.

• Build the recipe. Subtask decomposition, stage classifiers, relative actions, action chunking, normalization. Everything that turns "we got 30% success" into "we got 99% success."

• Push the data pipeline upstream so that fine-tuning is repeatable across robots and tasks, not a one-off.

RL on top of VLAs

• Residual policies for high-precision sub-movements (key insertion, peg-in-hole, force-sensitive contact).

• RL-driven training loops on top of VLAs and WAMs.

• Sim-to-real where it accelerates a real customer task, not for its own sake.

World models and synthetic data

• Build the workflow that turns a small amount of real teleop into a much larger training corpus.

• Decide what's worth using in our platform and what isn't.

• You'll own model side end to end: data, training, inference, evaluation, iteration.

Who we're looking for:

Required

• Strong research track record OR strong applied robotics ML track record. Either path works.

• Hands-on with at least one VLA stack. Trained one, evaluated one, debugged one. Not just read the paper.

• Comfortable with the main ML frameworks. Comfortable on Linux. Comfortable on a real robot (or eager to be).

• Comfortable with messy data and the realization that 80% of the work is making the data not lie to you.

• Comfortable shipping. Models in production beat models in arxiv at this company.

Bonus

• Real teleoperation or data collection experience

• RL beyond toy environments

• Experience with sim-to-real, world models, or video-conditioned generation

• Familiarity with VLAs

• You've shipped a robot policy that a non-engineer used and didn't break

What we don't care about

• Whether you have a PhD or you don't

• Whether you've worked at a famous lab or you haven't

• Whether your background is industry, academia, or self-taught

We care that you've done the thing.

How we work

• Small team, fast loop. Around 10 people. Repos move fast. No PR purgatory.

• Real customers from day one. You'll talk to pilots directly.

• Strong opinions, loosely held. We argue, we ship, we update. You'll be expected to push back when we're wrong.

• Hardware is real. Open Arm, R1 Light, Flexiv's, Thors. Not just sim.

What we offer

• Competitive salary + meaningful equity (early-stage)

• Working on robotics foundation models with a team that ships

• Direct line to founders and customers

• Copenhagen office, Stockholm satellite opening end of summer

• Real budget for compute, hardware, and other things that matter

• The usual good stuff

Apply here and or email fabian@qualiastudios.dev with whatever best represents your work and/or a resume.

jobs.description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management and Department of Biology, invites applicants for three two-year Postdoc positions within forest microbiome manipulation. The positions are part of the project “MycoForest - Stimulating Forest carbon uptake and storage by mycorrhizal inoculation”, which is financed under the Innomission partnership INNO-CCUS by Innovation Fund Denmark.
 
 Start date is 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The project
 The soil microbiome plays a crucial role in soil- and ecosystem functioning including ecosystem carbon sequestration and support of plant nutrient acquisition.
 
 Denmark is devoted to become carbon neutral by 2045/2050, a goal involving a significant role for biological carbon sequestration and storage. A part of the Danish strategy to reach carbon neutrality is to afforest former agricultural land thereby increasing biological ecosystem carbon capture and storage. However, agricultural soils do not harbor an optimal microbiome for initial tree growth and forest ecosystem development. This may lead to increased mortality, reduced tree growth and slower development of forest soil functions and ultimately non-optimal carbon capture, especially in the early stages of afforestation.
 
 Therefore, the MycoForest project aims to manipulate and assist the microbiome of agricultural soils through mycorrhizal inoculation as an integrated part of tree planting to stimulate tree growth and carbon sequestration. Therefore, MycoForest at University of Copenhagen is hiring three postdocs to become part of this novel journey towards increased biological carbon sequestration and to play key roles in the scientific investigations.
 
 Each of the three postdocs will cover one of three distinct areas of fundamental importance to understand and document the role of the microbiome in afforestation.
 
 The three key areas are:

   	
• Microbial and mycorrhizal fungal development 	
• Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics 	
• Tree survival and growth, and carbon uptake   
 The studies will involve controlled greenhouse as well as field scale experiments, and the three postdocs will each be responsible for one of the three specific parts of the project. At the same time, they will be closely linked to each other through tight collaboration on establishment and sampling of the afforestation experiment. The postdoc positions will start as soon as possible and will run for 2 years. For the requirements of the specific postdocs, please see the descriptions below.
 
 Contact: Specific questions for each of the postdocs, please see below. For general MycoForest questions, please contact Claus Beier, cbe@ign.ku.dk.
 
 Postdoc 1 – Soil microbial development after mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will oversee the formulation and addition of fungal or other types of inoculums and will follow and quantify the mycorrhizal fungal colonization of seedlings, root and soil. Experimentation will be both in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions and in the field. Colonization will be followed in different soils and host trees with a combination of classical microscopic techniques and novel molecular methods. The studies aim to document successful establishment of mycorrhizal fungi within the indigenous communities.
 
 Therefore, we are looking for candidates with specific knowledge and hands-on with:

   	
• Fungi in general including mycorrhizal fungi, preferentially ectomycorrhiza 	
• Field experience in general, handling and sorting soils and roots in specific 	
• Microscopy, especially stereo microscopy of roots 	
• DNA extraction og plants and soil and PCR optimizations including qPCR 	
• Bioinformatics and statistical analysis of meta-barcoding datasets   
 The post doc will work closely together with PD 2 and 3 for plant and soil responses to inoculations.
 
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Rasmus Kjøller, Department of Biology, rasmusk@bio.ku.dk, Phone: +45 35322311
 
 Postdoc 2 – Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics in response to mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will study effects of inoculation in different soil types and tree species on soil carbon processes including formation of persistent SOC fractions.  The postdoc will study soil carbon dynamics in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions in close cooperation with postdoc 1 and in field experimental conditions in cooperation with postdoc 3. The project will address how inoculation and changes in the mycorrhizal community composition will affect soil carbon sequestration processes in post-agricultural soils. The studies will shed light on the extent to which inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil will change the soil C input quantity and quality from roots and microbial necromass, eventually enhancing accumulation of persistent forms of SOC. 
 
 We are looking for a candidate with a PhD in the fields of soil science and organic matter studies, soil ecology and biogeochemistry. Previous experience with plant-soil interactions in field, mesocosm and laboratory experiments using chemical soil analyses including soil organic carbon (organic matter fractionation and biomarkers targeting microbial and plant origin of organic matter), carbon isotopes, roots, and microbial taxonomic and functional community composition will be considered a plus.
 
 Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Vesterdal, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, lv@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 61670865
 
 Postdoc 3 – Tree responses to mycorrhiza inoculation
 The postdoc will establish and follow field experiments in practical afforestation sites and monitor plant responses such as growth and survival, mycorrhizal colonization, and plant community development.
 
 The studies will address the potential of inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil to stimulate survival, growth and carbon draw down of forest trees and communities including the role of tree species and soil type interactions. 
 
 We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a PhD in plant or forestry science and interest and experience in:

   	
• Afforestation, forestry and forest ecology 	
• Design and analysis of experiments 	
• Field work and practical application of technology in land management    
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Niclas Scott Bentsen, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, nb@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 20206318.
 
 General qualifications
 Apart from the specific qualifications and interests listed above, we look for candidates with general competences in:

   	
• Driver license (mandatory) 	
• Handling of plants and soil 	
• Organizing and conducting field sampling 	
• Data management 	
• Statistics 	
• Scientific writing and publishing   
 Our groups and research – and what do we offer?
 The positions are located in three different groups at the university.
 
 Postdoc 1 is with Department of Biology, Fungal Ecology lab within Section of Terrestrial Ecology. The group works with/focuses on mycorrhizal fungal communities and their impact on ecosystem processes and plant health. We apply molecular markers to disentangle these otherwise invisible fungal populations and communities associated with plants and soil. Besides molecular markers, we also apply biochemical markers as well as classic microscopy and microbiological culturing of fungi. Another methodological strongpoint is various mesh-enclosure techniques to study and compartmentalize both the function and community composition of mycorrhizal fungal mycelia in soil.
 
 Postdoc 2 and 3 are with Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, one in the Biogeochemistry group and one in the Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group. In the Biogeochemistry Group we are dedicated to improving the understanding of ecosystem functioning with particular focus on how ecosystems will respond to environmental changes and to management actions. We quantify the pools and fluxes of matter in semi-natural and managed ecosystems and measure the processes related to input and output fluxes in control of soil C stocks to answer questions such as “Can we sequester C in soils by afforestation of cropland soils, and how does this interact with the soil fauna and microbes when using certain tree species or tree species mixtures?” The Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group encompas expertise in forestry, ecological restoration, growth modelling and systems analysis. The group is dedicated to advance the understanding, development, and management of forest ecosystems to support a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon storage, material and energy provision, groundwater regulation, and biodiversity conservation.
 
 Department of Biology is located at Norre Campus and Department of Geosciences on Frederiksberg Campus, close to central Copenhagen. The departments offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environments. The departments are planning to increase their focus on the climate change mitigation potential of forests in upcoming projects. We therefore welcome applications from candidates with a broader interest in the intersection of forests, forest-based climate solutions, biosphere-atmosphere interaction, and related themes.
 
 Responsibilities and tasks

   	
• Carry out independent research projects under the PI’s supervision and in close collaboration with the other PostDocs and researchers within the MycoForest project. 	
• Report and disseminate the periodic progress and results 	
• Take part in relevant teaching activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at relevant journals 	
• Actively take part in the research environments at the departments, sections and within the project.   
 We are looking for the following further qualifications:

   	
• Strong ability to interpret data and think analytically, critically, and conceptually. 	
• Strong social competence including interpersonal skills, teamwork and networking ability, and presentation skills 	
• Strong personal competence including autonomy, goal-oriented mind-set, planning/organizing/prioritizing, perseverance, problem-solving skills 	
• General personal leadership skills including ability to translate long-term goals to daily work situations (strategic time managing); be flexible to adjust one’s own behavior and thinking according to the (relevant/local) context so as to attain the desired goals (learning ability) 	
• Good language skills and fluency in English   
 Terms of employment
 Employment is full-time and for 2 years.
 
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.
 
 Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.
 
 Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.
 
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).
 
 Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and indicate which of the 3 positions you are applying for.
 
 The application is submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.
 
 Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) – please relate how the above required abilities are represented in your past work experiences 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or master’s and PhD and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list 	
• Reference letters (if available)   
 Application deadline:
 The deadline for applications is 2 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.
 
 The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.
 
 The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.
 
 Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 49-50 2026.
 
 Applicants must be prepared for further security screening related to international research collaborations as part of the recruitment process, when UCPH considers it appropriate from a holistic consideration
